detections.name: Linux SSH failure burst
detections.description: Repeated sshd authentication failures from one source IP inside 120 seconds.
detections.falsePositives: A person mistypes a password six times from one host. Several people behind one NAT address look like one source.
detections.tuningNotes: frequency 6 and timeframe 120. Stock rules 5712 and 5763 use frequency 8. Raise the frequency if lab users regularly mistype this often.
detections.testProcedure: make logtest ID=SF-013. Six synthetic failures from 10.10.10.200 must fire. Five must not.
detections.expectedEvent: sshd Failed password or invalid user from one source IP, six times in 120 seconds.
detections.expectedAlert: Description starts with SF-013. Rule 100701 or 100702, level 10.
detections.wazuhRuleXml:
<rule id="100701" level="10" frequency="6" timeframe="120" ignore="60">
    <if_matched_sid>5710</if_matched_sid>
    <same_source_ip />
    <description>SF-013: sshd invalid-user failure burst from one source IP</description>
    <mitre>
      <id>T1110.001</id>
    </mitre>
    <group>sentinelforge,linux,</group>
  </rule>

<rule id="100702" level="10" frequency="6" timeframe="120" ignore="60">
    <!-- 5760 is the alert id for "Failed password" (if_sid 5716). 5716 itself is not the fired id. -->
    <if_matched_sid>5760</if_matched_sid>
    <same_source_ip />
    <description>SF-013: sshd authentication-failure burst from one source IP</description>
    <mitre>
      <id>T1110.001</id>
    </mitre>
    <group>sentinelforge,linux,</group>
  </rule>
detections.sigmaYaml:
title: SF-013 sshd failure burst from one source IP
id: 7c1a0e2b-4d55-4a1e-9f30-0b6c2a8e13d1
status: experimental
description: >
  sshd authentication failure. The six-event, 120 second, same-source threshold
  lives in Wazuh rules 100701 and 100702. This selection is the single-event
  equivalent.
logsource:
  product: linux
  service: sshd
detection:
  selection:
    - 'invalid user'
    - 'Failed password'
  condition: selection
level: medium
tags:
  - attack.credential_access
  - attack.t1110.001
falsepositives:
  - A user mistypes a password.

detections.name: Linux SSH success after failures
detections.description: sshd authentication success from a source IP that just produced an SF-013 failure burst.
detections.falsePositives: A person mistypes a password six times and then succeeds. That is the detection. Shared jump hosts make it noisier.
detections.tuningNotes: Fires only after SF-013 (100701 or 100702) in the same 120 second window and from the same source IP. Level 12.
detections.testProcedure: make logtest ID=SF-014. Six failures then Accepted password from 10.10.10.200 must fire. Five failures then a success must not.
detections.expectedEvent: sshd Accepted password from the same source IP after six failures inside 120 seconds.
detections.expectedAlert: Description starts with SF-014. Rule 100710 or 100711, level 12. MITRE T1078 only.
detections.wazuhRuleXml:
<rule id="100710" level="12" frequency="2" timeframe="120">
    <if_sid>5715</if_sid>
    <if_matched_sid>100701</if_matched_sid>
    <same_source_ip />
    <description>SF-014: sshd success after invalid-user failures from the same source IP</description>
    <mitre>
      <id>T1078</id>
    </mitre>
    <group>sentinelforge,linux,</group>
  </rule>

<rule id="100711" level="12" frequency="2" timeframe="120">
    <if_sid>5715</if_sid>
    <if_matched_sid>100702</if_matched_sid>
    <same_source_ip />
    <description>SF-014: sshd success after authentication failures from the same source IP</description>
    <mitre>
      <id>T1078</id>
    </mitre>
    <group>sentinelforge,linux,</group>
  </rule>
detections.sigmaYaml:
title: SF-014 sshd success after a failure burst
id: 2f9b6c44-8a17-4c3e-b5d0-11e7a4c014e2
status: experimental
description: >
  sshd authentication success. The requirement that SF-013 already fired from
  the same source IP inside 120 seconds lives in Wazuh rules 100710 and 100711.
  This selection is the success line only.
logsource:
  product: linux
  service: sshd
detection:
  selection:
    - 'Accepted password'
    - 'Accepted publickey'
  condition: selection
level: high
tags:
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.t1078
falsepositives:
  - A normal login with no recent failures. The Wazuh rule does not alert on that line alone.
